brief.ask: Set the art direction for 36 high-end wedding evites as a coherent luxury line, not 36 one-offs. Decide the families (we explored watercolor botanicals, painted Italian villas, art deco emerald and gold) and what the motion layer does that paper never could, without becoming a gimmick.
brief.audience: Couples choosing a stationery suite; guests from 20 to 90.
brief.feeling: The weight of letterpress and the light of a candlelit room, in a phone.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.
Must sit beside the best paper stationery studios and win.
references: Exploration grid A: fine-art watercolor garden roses, peonies, olive and eucalyptus forming arches on deckled cotton paper with gold-foil flecks; flat-lay on silk and brass trays.
Exploration grid B: gouache Italian villa terraces, arched colonnades, cypress, lemon trees in terracotta, bougainvillea, golden-hour hills.
Exploration grid C: deep emerald marble with art deco gold linework frames, crescent moons and fine constellations; symmetrical and grand.

proposals.title: The Canonical Line
proposals.idea: Thirty-six designs governed by one proportional system — a golden-section page canon derived from incunabula layout — so that every family reads as chapters of a single illuminated codex, not a collection of moods.
proposals.geometry: Page canon after Van de Graaf: the live-text block occupies the canonical rectangle inscribed within the phone viewport at 390px, with margins in 2:3:4:6 ratio (inner:top:outer:bottom), giving the text field the same weight a compositor would have cut into a letterpress chase. The art plate bleeds to full bleed only in the upper third; the lower two-thirds is structurally protected white space that the eye earns by descending through the composition. All three families — botanical, villa, deco — are proportioned to this same canon; what distinguishes them is the character of the art within the fixed measure, never the measure itself. The deco family uses the canon as the explicit revealed object: the gold linework *is* the grid, made visible.
proposals.typography: Primary: Freight Display Pro (italic for names, roman for date and venue) — it carries the weight of a hot-metal face without demanding a press. Secondary: Freight Text Pro for all detail lines. Neither face is swapped between families; instead, optical size and leading are the only variables — 72pt/84pt leading for names, 13pt/20pt leading for venue copy, all set in a 16-unit baseline grid locked to the page canon. No display face from a trend cycle; Freight has seventeen years of editorial proof. Small caps for venue names only, tracked at +60. Zero decorative typefaces — the art carries ornament; the type carries information.
proposals.imageLogic: Each art plate is an original large-format painting commissioned at 6000×9000px minimum — watercolor on 640gsm Fabriano Artistico for the botanical family, gouache on gesso board for the villa family, and gilded ink on black Canson for the deco family — then drum-scanned, not flatbed-scanned, so the tooth of the paper and the pooling of pigment read at full zoom. The scan is the image; no stock, no generative fill. Foreground cut-out layers are isolated from the same painting — a rose cluster, a cypress branch, a single constellation arc — so the depth stack is native to the artwork, not composited from separate sources. The link-preview crop is determined at commission time: the painter is briefed on a specific 1200×628px region that must read as a self-contained image.
proposals.texture: The painting surface is the texture: Fabriano cold-press tooth, gesso craquelure, the granulation of ultramarine pooling in a wet wash. These are captured in the drum scan and never simulated with a Photoshop overlay. The WebGL foil layer reads as a second texture — not a filter applied to the art, but a separate mask-revealed plane that catches light the way a real die-stamped foil catches it: directionally, with a slight lag, so it appears to sit *above* the paper rather than printed onto it. Candle-flicker particles in the botanical family are sub-pixel, not bokeh circles — they behave like the refraction of a crystal glass, not a lens.
proposals.motion: Sequence and governance are everything: stillness first, always. The card loads static — full art, full text, readable — for 1.2 seconds before any motion begins. This is not a transition delay; it is a deliberate rest, the way a Haydn exposition states the theme before development. Then, in order: (1) the foil shimmer plane activates on a 0.4-second ease-in, directional to ambient light via device orientation — if reduced-motion is flagged, this layer is suppressed entirely and the card remains beautiful; (2) the foreground cut-out layer drifts 4–8px on phone tilt, with a 180ms lag and 12px max displacement — parallax at the scale of breath, not of animation; (3) candle-flicker or bokeh particles pulse at 0.3Hz, irregular, never looping at a detectable interval. Nothing announces itself. A guest at 80 sees a still, luminous card; a guest at 25 discovers the depth. The motion layer does
proposals.productionMethod: Commission a core studio of three painters — one botanical specialist, one architectural gouachist, one decorative-arts gilding artist — under a Plajah work-for-hire agreement that covers all 36 plates. Each painter delivers 12 plates in their medium. Drum scans at 1200dpi by a repro house (not in-house). Tela document structure: Layer 0 = drum-scan art plate (full bleed, static); Layer 1 = isolated foreground cut-outs (PNG with alpha, drift-reactive); Layer 2 = WebGL mask plane (foil/flicker/bokeh, orientation-reactive); Layer 3 = live Tela text (Freight, never baked). The page canon is a shared Tela template; all 36 designs inherit it. Families are distinguished by a Tela 'style token' that swaps art plate, cut-out set, and WebGL preset without touching the text layer or the grid.
proposals.humanTrace: The drum-scanned painting is the irreducible human trace: you can see where the watercolor bloomed at the edge of a wet passage, where the gouache was lifted with a dry brush to reveal the gesso beneath, where the gilding was burnished unevenly because a hand applied the leaf. These are not imperfections to be retouched; they are the proof of making that justifies the luxury price point. The foil shimmer is the only synthetic element, and it is masked to follow the actual gilded regions in the deco plates — so even the WebGL effect is anchored to a physical gesture.
proposals.risk: The risk is commissioning cost and timeline: twelve plates per painter, drum-scan repro, and a strict no-stock rule means the line cannot be assembled cheaply or quickly. The counter-argument is that a line built on one proportional canon and three genuine painted traditions will hold its authority for a decade, where a trend-assembled collection expires in two years. The secondary risk is that the page canon reads as rigid to a couple who want something idiosyncratic — but I would argue that idiosyncrasy lives in the painting, not the grid, and that a grid that holds is what allows the painting to breathe.

arguesWith.why: The Futurist will propose that the template system be generative — that couples can tune parameters and the layout responds. I am directly opposed: a layout that reconfigures on user input is a layout that cannot be read twice the same way, and legibility across a guest range of 20 to 90, on a phone browser, without a sign-up, requires that the compositional hierarchy be fixed and unconditional. proposals.title: Ink Before the Screen
proposals.idea: Every design in the line is anchored to a physically made master plate — linocut, woodblock, or screen-printed monoprint — so the motion layer acts as candlelight falling across an object that already exists, not a simulation of one.
proposals.geometry: Portrait, 390px wide, structured on a 12-unit baseline grid locked to the physical plate's registration marks — intentional misalignment of up to 4px between plate layer and foreground cutouts mirrors the natural drift of hand-pulled prints; no element bleeds perfectly to edge; a narrow unprinted margin on all four sides reads as the deckle.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond Italic for names and venue — cut at large scale, letterspaced tight, carrying its own historical weight without seriffing to death. Secondary: a single weight of Neue Haas Grotesk Display Roman for dates and times — blunt, factual, a compositor's label glued to the back of a painting. No mixing of more than two families per card. Case: sentence case throughout, never all-caps, because a hand-addressed envelope never shouts.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs of flowers or villas. Instead: high-resolution scans of the actual carved block or screen — ink fills, ghost ink, tool-mark shadows — are the art plate layer. The Tela art plate is a 4800dpi scan flattened to a web-optimized file; the grain is real grain, not a filter. Foreground cutouts are isolated elements from the same scan, masked so the torn paper edge or squeegee drag is visible at the cutout boundary.
proposals.texture: The base layer is the scanned print — indigo, ochre, or alizarin on unsized Japanese kozo paper or Fabriano Rosaspina depending on the family. The WebGL foil shimmer is applied only inside the recessed ink channels (where the block pressed hardest), making the shimmer behave like gilding pressed into a letterpress deboss — it lives in the dent, not on the surface. Bokeh particles float above at extreme shallow depth, sourced from photographed candlelight through a macro lens.
proposals.motion: On open: the plate sits still for 800ms — the pause before a candle is lit. Then a single candle-flicker light leak moves from bottom-left corner outward, revealing the foil shimmer in the ink channels only where the light 'reaches'. Phone tilt shifts the foreground cutout elements (a sprig, a single bloom, a cypress silhouette) at parallax depth — slow, 0.3x tilt ratio, never more than 14px travel, so a 70-year-old guest does not feel motion-sick. No looping animation; the card breathes once, then holds. Reduced motion: all animation removed; the foil shimmer is replaced with a static gold tint at 60% opacity on the ink channels only — the card is still beautiful, just still.
proposals.productionMethod: 1. Artist carves a master block or burns a screen for each of the three families (botanical, villa, deco geometric) — one block per family, with variant colorways achieved by ink swap, not new carving. 2. Pulls are made on paper; best pull is selected and scanned at 4800dpi. 3. Scan is composited in Tela as the locked art plate. 4. Individual botanical or architectural elements are isolated from the same scan as transparent foreground cutouts — no redrawing, no vector tracing, the torn edge is kept. 5. WebGL mask is hand-painted as a luminosity map in Procreate, exported as greyscale PNG — it tells the foil layer where the ink channels are. 6. Live text fields placed by Tela template system; names and dates never touch the art layer.
proposals.humanTrace: The ink channel. Where the block pressed hardest, ink is thicker, edges feather into the paper fiber. That physical fact — pressure — is what the WebGL foil reads as its mask. If you zoom to 200% on the phone you see the paper grain under the ink. The tool mark is not decoration; it is the load-bearing structure of the entire motion layer.
proposals.risk: Couples paying for luxury expect perfection. A visible registration drift, a squeegee ghost, a slightly uneven ink edge — these read as mistakes to half the market and as authenticity to the other half. We are betting on the half that knows the difference between a letterpress card and a digital imitation of one. We also risk slow perception of load — the 4800dpi scan must compress without losing the grain, which is technically hard. That risk is worth it because no competitor is doing this: they are all simulating texture; we are starting with the thing itself.

arguesWith.why: The Futurist will want to generate the plate algorithmically — procedural woodgrain, parametric botanical forms — and will argue it scales better across 36 designs. I say: simulation is not making. A parametric woodgrain has no grain direction because no wood was cut. proposals.title: State Machines for Ceremony
proposals.idea: Each design is a rule-governed simulation of physical light passing through layered translucent matter — the card never exists; what exists is a physics model that responds to the phone's sensor inputs and produces a different luminous state every second it is held.
proposals.geometry: Three structural families sharing one underlying grid: a 4×7 modular column system at 390px locks all type and art to the same harmonic intervals. Family A (Botanical) uses a vertical axis with asymmetric bleed panels — art plate fills 60% height, foreground cutouts break into the top 15% and bottom 25%, creating a portal rather than a frame. Family B (Villa) uses a horizon-line rule at the golden ratio (61.8% from top), architecture sits below, sky and light above; the rule never moves but the light above it does. Family C (Deco) uses strict bilateral symmetry about a single vertical spine, with a radial subdivision for the central medallion; all linework is generated from the same parametric rule set so the 12 Deco cards are literally one system rendered at 12 different initial conditions, not 12 separate drawings.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond Italic for names and headline — its ink-trap geometry holds at small sizes and its optical weight reads as engraved without faking engraving. Secondary: Optima Nova Regular for all logistical text (date, venue, time) — it is humanist without being calligraphic, legible at 12px on a dim screen. Tertiary: a single weight of Neue Haas Grotesk Display for system-state UI micro-labels if any interactive affordance needs labeling. Case: names in title case, all venue and date lines in tracked small-caps at 80% optical size. No script faces — the motion layer is the calligraphic gesture; the type does not need to perform it.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All art is generated from physical source material that has been scanned at 1200dpi and then subjected to a rule: watercolors are scanned wet, mid-bloom, so the pigment boundary is still moving at capture — the diffusion edge becomes the data the shader reads to animate the bloom in real time. Gouache villa panels are painted on gessoed board, photographed under a single raking light source at three angles (0°, 22°, 45°), and the three captures are blended by the WebGL layer as a function of gyroscope pitch — so the raking light tracks the phone's physical orientation. The Deco marble is a real slab photographed, not a texture tile; the gold linework is plotted on a pen plotter over a print of the marble scan, re-photographed, and composited as a separate alpha channel. Every image has a documented physical origin; the shader is the second author, not the first.
proposals.texture: The base texture contract for all 36: deckled paper edge is a signed distance field mask applied to the art plate, not a raster image — it scales without aliasing and responds to the foil shimmer layer passing through it. The shimmer layer is a WebGL iridescent BRDF (bidirectional reflectance distribution function) with roughness driven by the scanned surface's luminance channel — rough watercolor tooth scatters the shimmer; smooth gouache concentrates it. Candle flicker is a Perlin noise field modulating an orange-amber point light at 0.3–1.2 Hz (measured from a real candle filmed at 240fps; the frequency distribution was extracted and baked into the noise parameters). This is not a loop; it is a simulation seeded differently each open.
proposals.motion: Motion is a state machine with four states, not an animation timeline. State 0 (Load): art plate fades from black in 800ms using an exponential ease — the image appears to develop, not dissolve. State 1 (Rest): foreground cutouts drift on a slow Lissajous path at 0.04Hz — perceptible only after 3 seconds of stillness; the card breathes, it does not animate. State 2 (Tilt-Active): gyroscope input maps to two outputs simultaneously — the foil BRDF specular highlight translates across the surface (parallax of a real foil card), and the raking-light blend shifts between the three Villa captures or rotates the Deco radial gradient; these are different physical simulations, not the same effect re-skinned. State 3 (Tap-Hold): bokeh particles (out-of-focus light discs, physically sized to match the implied depth of field of the art) rise from the lower third at 12 particles/second, peak at 40 on
proposals.productionMethod: Each of the three families is built as a parameterized Tela template, not 12 separate documents. A single GLSL shader file per family accepts uniform inputs (gyro XY, time, seed, family-specific texture samplers) and produces all visual states. The art plates for all 36 are produced in four physical sessions: two watercolor painting days (Botanical family), one gouache painting day (Villa), one marble photography and pen-plotter session (Deco). Scans and photographs are processed through a documented pipeline — no AI generation of the art itself; AI is used only to extract frequency data from the candle footage. The foreground cutout layer for each card is hand-masked from the scanned art, preserving scan artifacts at edges. Live text (names, dates, venue) is injected via Tela's data layer and never touches the shader.
proposals.humanTrace: The diffusion boundary of a wet watercolor bloom, captured mid-movement at 1200dpi, is the shader's animation data — the imperfection is not added; it is the source. The three raking-light photographs of each gouache panel are taken by a person holding a single LED panel at measured angles; the parallax the guest feels on tilt is the parallax a photographer felt in the room. The pen plotter's mechanical slop — the 0.3mm line-start hesitation visible on the gold linework — is preserved in the alpha channel and visible at 2× zoom. These are not stylistic choices; they are the physical record of the making process, present in the file.
proposals.risk: The risk is that guests and couples read the tilt-responsive light as a technical trick rather than a material truth — that the physics model feels like a gimmick precisely because it is working correctly, because people are not accustomed to a wedding card that is also an instrument. The counter-argument is that letterpress's weight was also a technical demonstration of a physical process — the impression in the paper is the machine proving it was there. This system makes the same argument in a different medium. The other risk is load performance on low-end Android; the mitigation is progressive enhancement — the card is designed to be complete at State 0, and every subsequent state is additive, never required.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want the particle event — State 3 — to be the opening move, autoplay on load, because spectacle should announce itself. I refuse this. A reveal without a rule is a screensaver. The particles are gated behind a tap-hold precisely because that interaction makes the guest a causal agent in the physics; the bokeh rises because they chose to hold the card still and ask it a q

proposals.title: Field-Documented, Maker-Named Luxury
proposals.idea: Each family is anchored to a specific documented making tradition — a named printmaker's block, a recorded garden, a mapped architectural site — so the digital shimmer traces real physical evidence and the line coheres as a collection of provenance, not a mood board.
proposals.geometry: Three families, each with a distinct structural logic that does not bleed between them. Family A (Botanical Archive): a single asymmetric arch column left-anchored, deckled edge implied by a scanned cotton-paper boundary running vertically at 72% width, text in the remaining 28% margin — portrait, never centered. Family B (Villa Topography): a horizon line fixed at the golden ratio (~61.8% from top), architecture below, sky above; a single vanishing point slightly left of center creating mild perspectival pull; text always above the horizon in the sky register. Family C (Cartographic Deco): a strict bilateral axis with a measured grid of 6×10 field units, all ornament snapping to that grid — no freehand deviation; text occupies the central 4 units wide.
proposals.typography: Family A: Cormorant Garamond Italic for names and key lines (its ink-trap details read as letterpress at small sizes), Cormorant SC for venue and date, tracked +80; no sans anywhere. Family B: Freight Display Pro Italic for the couple's names set large, Freight Text for details, all lines ranged left, never centered, to echo handwritten villa-guest-book entries. Family C: Optima Nova (Zapf, 1958 revival) for all caps headers — its flared terminals echo deco without pastiche — paired with a condensed geometric mono (Martian Mono) for date/time data, creating a deliberate tension between ornament and precision. All three families: minimum 17px body on mobile, generous leading at 1.6, never white text on a textured background without a tested contrast ratio above 4.5:1.
proposals.imageLogic: No stock. Family A: scanned physical art plates made from original block-prints by a named maker (collaboration-gated — I am flagging this now to the team: if we use any specific regional botanical block-print tradition, e.g. Bagru or Kutch, we need a paid collaboration and credited maker, not a vibe-lift). Failing that, original watercolor botanicals commissioned from a specific illustrator whose name appears in the Tela metadata. Family B: documentary photographs of actual Italian villa gardens — I propose a licensed archive from a named photographer, or original field photography, with GPS coordinates logged in production notes; the images are treated as tonal underlays desaturated to warm umber, never filtered into a generic 'golden hour preset.' Family C: no photography; pure vector geometry derived from scanned period-accurate deco ornament books (Dover republications are public do
proposals.texture: Family A: a high-resolution scan of actual 300gsm cotton-rag paper (Fabriano Artistico rough, scanned at 1200dpi, cleared for digital use) forms the base plate; the deckled edge is a real scan, not a Photoshop brush. Gold flecks are WebGL particles whose spawn positions are locked to the physical paper scan's fiber-density map — they cannot appear where the paper is smooth. Family B: a scanned aged-fresco plaster texture (sourced from a photographed wall, location documented) sits under the gouache layer as a very low-opacity multiply; the gouache itself is original painted art, not a filter. Family C: emerald is a photographed marble slab (specific quarry noted in production; I want Connemara marble considered — Irish, documented, visually distinct from generic 'luxury green') with the WebGL foil layer gated entirely by the physical veining topology, per my standing rule: digital luster
proposals.motion: Motion is a single slow breath per family, not a sequence of effects. Family A: on load, the botanical foreground cutouts drift 4px on the tilt axis over 2.8 seconds with a sine ease — as if a breeze crossed the page; the gold-fleck particles rise at 0.3px/s against gravity, pausing when the phone is still. No loop; they settle. Family B: the horizon layer has a 0.6% parallax offset from the sky layer on tilt, creating depth without animation; a single candle-flicker light leak pulses at 0.04Hz in the lower-left corner — almost imperceptible, felt more than seen. Family C: the deco gold linework traces itself once on first open over 1.4 seconds (stroke-draw animation along the SVG path), then rests; the constellation dots blink at randomized 4–9s intervals, like actual stars. All motion: reduced-motion respected; static fallback shows the fully-composed plate with no animation, still jaw
proposals.productionMethod: Each family produced as a Tela layered document: (1) art plate — high-res raster, pre-composited, exported at 2× for retina; (2) foreground cutouts — PNG with real transparency, individually masked in Tela; (3) WebGL effects layer — a single shared shader per family, parameters (particle density, flicker frequency, foil threshold) exposed as Tela variables so the 12 designs within each family differ in intensity without requiring 12 separate shaders; (4) live text layer — Tela native, never baked, couple's names/dates/venues editable by the Plajah user; (5) link preview — a static 1200×630 render of the art plate at its most legible moment, generated server-side. Production notes file per design cites: maker name, source scan location, date acquired, license or collaboration agreement reference.
proposals.humanTrace: The cotton-paper fiber map that governs particle spawn (Family A); the single vanishing-point perspective drawn from a documented photograph, not generated (Family B); the hand-inked ornament source plate number and the physical veining topology that gates the WebGL foil (Family C). In every case, a person's hand or a specific physical object is upstream of every digital effect. The WebGL layer cannot invent texture; it can only reveal or echo what the physical source already contains.
proposals.risk: The provenance requirement will slow production and may require paid collaborations that increase cost per family. Some couples will not see or care about the maker attribution buried in metadata. The risk is worth it because: (a) a line built on specific, documented sources ages well and cannot be accused of appropriation after launch; (b) the physical-source constraint on the WebGL layer produces shimmer that looks materially different from every competitor's generic foil preset — it is the specificity that makes it luxury, not the gold color; (c) if the Futurist's code is constrained by real topography, as I saw work with the indigo block-print scan, the result is technically and aesthetically superior to unconstrained generative shimmer.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will reach for maximum richness in all three families simultaneously — gold in A, gold in B, gold in C — and will want the motion to crescendo. I will hold the line that each family earns its one register of grandeur and that the WebGL foil is rationed, not maximized. Borrowed grandeur that ignores whose textile, whose marble, whose ornament tradition is being quoted is not luxury; i

proposals.title: The Curtain Before the Ceremony
proposals.idea: Each evite is a miniature opera in three acts — darkness, reveal, radiance — staged through chiaroscuro light that rises like a candle being carried into a room, so the guest experiences arrival before they read a single word.
proposals.geometry: Portrait format locked to a 390px stage. A single dominant vertical axis — the spine of a proscenium — divides the composition asymmetrically: 60% deep shadow field, 40% illuminated subject. Botanical or architectural elements are never centered; they lean in from one wing, cut by the frame edge, implying a world larger than the phone. The text block sits in a controlled pool of light at the lower third, as though set on a conductor's lectern. Three families share this geometry: (A) the arched garden — a floral colonnade that frames the text pool from above; (B) the villa terrace — a receding perspective colonnade with depth planes staggered vertically; (C) the deco altar — a symmetrical mandorla of gold linework that collapses into the text pool at its nadir. Same stage, three sets.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond Italic for names and headline — its ink-trap corners catch the shimmer layer and read as letterpress bite at small sizes. Cormorant SC for venue and date lines in tight tracked small caps, set at 11–12px equivalent, never condensed. A single weight of Freight Text Pro for body copy where needed — warm, editorial, human. No sans-serif anywhere in the suite; this is not a tech product. All caps forbidden except the venue line. Leading generous: 1.5× body, 1.2× display. The type is always live Tela text — never baked — and sits above the WebGL layer so it is always the last thing the light touches.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. All art plates are original painted works — gouache and ink on hot-press board for the villa family; wet watercolor on 300gsm cold-press with salt-drop texture for the botanical family; gouache with gold-leaf pressed flat and then scanned at 1200dpi for the deco family. The scan is the source of truth: every digital artifact — the paper grain, the bleeding edge of a petal, the cracked margin of a gold-leaf sheet — is preserved and becomes the texture layer. Nothing is reconstructed in 3D. The painted plate occupies the background layer; foreground cut-out elements (a single branch, a leaning cypress, a crescent arc) are isolated on transparent layers and given the tilt-reactive drift. The painting is the anchor; the motion makes it breathe.
proposals.texture: The background plate carries visible paper tooth — the cold-press watercolor families show salt-crystal pitting and tide-line blooms; the deco family shows the micro-fracture pattern of genuine gold leaf at its edges. A WebGL normal-map is derived from the scanned paper grain so that the foil shimmer layer physically follows the texture of the original sheet — when you tilt the phone, the shimmer travels along the actual ridges of the cotton paper. This is not a filter applied to a flat image; it is a light simulation anchored to a real material surface. The candle-flicker particle layer adds 4–6 soft bokeh points at f/1.4 equivalent blur, positioned asymmetrically in the shadow field, never in the text pool.
proposals.motion: Act One — darkness. The evite opens on 80% of its final luminosity suppressed; the art plate is visible but dim, like a room before the candles are lit. Duration: 600ms hold, no movement, reduced-motion users land here and stay — this is also the static state. Act Two — the carry. A warm point-light source rises from below-frame at the pace of someone walking toward a table: 1.8 seconds, eased with a cubic-bezier that hesitates twice — one mechanical stutter at 40%, one at 75% — because candlelight is not smooth and I refuse to let it be. The light pool expands from the text zone upward, revealing the painting incrementally. The foreground cut-out elements drift 6–12px on their vertical axis in response to phone tilt, with a 200ms lag — they are heavier than air. Act Three — radiance. At full luminosity, the foil shimmer activates on the gold elements: a single slow oscillation, 3-second
proposals.productionMethod: 1. Commission original painted art plates — three painters, one per family, working on physical media. Specify the substrate, pigment family, and required scan resolution in the brief. The botanical painter works wet-on-wet watercolor; the villa painter works layered gouache with turpentine washes for atmosphere; the deco painter works gouache over gold-leaf on black gesso. 2. Scan at 1200dpi; extract normal maps from the grain channel using Substance or equivalent. 3. Isolate foreground elements in Photoshop with manual masking — no AI cutouts; the edge quality must be painterly, not clean. 4. Build each Tela document with: background plate at full bleed, normal-map-driven WebGL shimmer layer, foreground tilt layer, candle-flicker particle layer, live text zone. 5. The 36 designs are 12 per family × 3 families; within each family, designs vary by: composition mirror, dominant hue temper
proposals.humanTrace: The salt-crystal pitting and tide-line blooms in the watercolor plates are unrepeatable — they are the record of water moving across paper on a specific afternoon. The gold-leaf fracture edges in the deco plates are the record of a hand pressing metal to gesso and peeling. The normal map is derived from these physical events. When the shimmer travels along the paper grain on a guest's phone, it is traveling along the memory of a painter's table.
proposals.risk: The painted-art-plate approach requires commissioning real painters and a production pipeline that is slower and more expensive than generating art. The risk is schedule and budget. It is worth it because the alternative — generated botanicals or stock villa photography — produces work that a $12 Canva template also produces, and we are not here to compete with Canva. The second risk is that the mechanical stutter in the candle-carry animation reads as a bug to users trained on fluid micro-interactions. I am willing to defend this choice: the stutter is the human trace in the motion layer. A flame does not ease-in-out. If we smooth it, we lose the thing that makes it feel like fire and not a progress bar.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will look at the three-act motion sequence and the layered WebGL stack and say we should choose one effect and let it breathe. I reject this on grounds of function, not taste. A guest opens this link once, on a phone, possibly in a noisy family group chat, with three seconds of attention before they scroll. proposals.title: The Architecture of Ceremony
proposals.idea: Strip each family to its single load-bearing contrast — one botanical silhouette against structural silence, one villa arch against compressed sky, one deco line against deep ground — so the WebGL light does not decorate but reveals, like a candle finding the only thing in the room worth finding.
proposals.geometry: 390px fixed column. Vertical thirds: top third is pure field — color or void — holding nothing but the art plate edge. Middle third: a single centered column, 280px wide, max. Text never bleeds to gutter. Bottom third: date and venue in one unbroken horizontal rule below which nothing lives. Grid is 8pt baseline throughout. Across all 36 designs the grid does not change; only the art plate and its mask change. The line is the constant. The families share one proportional skeleton.
proposals.typography: Primary: Cormorant Garamond Italic Light — long ascenders, deliberate fragility, earns every pixel at 28px headline. Secondary label: Optima Regular, tracked at +120, caps, 9px — the only sans, used once per card for the couple's names as a hairline counterpoint. Date: Cormorant Garamond Regular, tabular figures, 13px, centered. No bold weight appears anywhere in the system. Hierarchy is built through scale and silence, not weight. Reduced-motion fallback collapses to static with identical typographic rhythm.
proposals.imageLogic: Art plates are generated at 1560×2x resolution as single painted or photographed originals — watercolor botanicals shot on cotton rag under raking natural sidelight, villa gouaches photographed on plaster rather than scanned, deco marble photographed from actual Verde Guatemala stone slabs — then masked to a shape that is always architecturally derived: an arch, a rectangle with one clipped corner, a strict oval. No full-bleed illustration. The art plate never touches the text column's left or right edges; minimum 16px air on each side. Foreground cut-outs — a single rose stem, a cypress, a crescent — are isolated on transparent layers and drift 3–6px on tilt, no more. The image earns its place by what it withholds as much as what it shows.
proposals.texture: Each family has one permitted texture register. Botanical family: deckled-edge mask on the art plate, rendered as a 1px feathered path, not a filter — the irregularity is drawn, not generated. Villa family: warm plaster grain applied as a 4% opacity multiply layer over the art plate only, never over text. Deco family: no applied texture; the Verde Guatemala marble photograph is the texture. Across all families: no gradients in the UI chrome. The texture lives only inside the art plate boundary. Outside the plate is silence.
proposals.motion: Three-beat sequence, total duration 2.2 seconds on open, then idle. Beat 1 — 0 to 0.6s: art plate fades from 0 to 100% opacity, linear, no easing curve theatrics. Beat 2 — 0.6 to 1.4s: WebGL foil or candle-flicker mask blooms from the geometric center of the plate outward, stopping at plate edge — it never crosses into the text field. The bloom is slow enough to read as breath, not flash. Beat 3 — 1.4 to 2.2s: text fades in one field at a time — couple names, then date, then venue — each 0.2s apart, opacity only, no translate. Idle: foreground cut-out drifts on gyroscope at 0.4px/degree, max 6px total travel, spring-damped. Candle-flicker WebGL runs at 24fps, amplitude capped so it never pulls the eye from the text. Reduced motion: all animation disabled; plate, foil layer, and text appear at 100% opacity on load simultaneously.
proposals.productionMethod: Each art plate is a physical original first: watercolor on Fabriano Artistico 300gsm, gouache on gesso board, or macro photograph of Verde Guatemala stone. Original is photographed under controlled sidelight with a Phase One or equivalent; retoucher removes support but preserves paper grain and paint edge. Tela document receives the plate as a high-res PNG with embedded transparency mask. Foreground cut-outs are traced from the same original by hand in Figma, exported as SVG, imported as Tela foreground layer. WebGL effects are parameterized — one shader file per family, three parameters exposed: bloom radius, flicker amplitude, foil density — so a production assistant can tune without touching code. Live text is a Tela text layer, never rasterized. Names, dates, venues are inserted by the couple at configuration; font renders live. QR and link-preview use a static first-frame export at
proposals.humanTrace: The deckled edge on the botanical plate is drawn as a closed path by a human hand in Figma using a Wacom tablet with pressure sensitivity on — the line weight varies 0.4 to 1.2px because of actual wrist pressure, not a brush preset. The rose stems in the foreground cut-out layer retain the original watercolor's visible wet-into-wet bloom at the petal base, photographed not filtered. The marble photograph shows one faint quarry saw-mark at the upper left corner of the slab; it remains in every deco design as proof of material, not as decoration.
proposals.risk: The risk is that restraint reads as emptiness to the couple comparing this against a maximalist competitor at thumbnail scale. The link-preview frame — one arch, one name, silence — may not convert without context. That risk is worth it because the couples this line is built for are choosing stationery, not content; they understand that a room with one candle is not an empty room. The silence is the luxury signal. If we fill it, we become every other evite.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will argue that the WebGL bloom should cross the plate boundary and wash over the text field on open — that the light leak is the emotional event and containing it to the art plate is timid. I disagree precisely. The moment the flicker touches the type, the type becomes decoration. The letterpress feeling the brief asks for comes from the separation of ink from ground — the type live

disputes.objection: The state machine is precisely the problem: a system that produces a different luminous state every second it is held cannot be read twice the same way, and a wedding invitation that cannot be re-experienced as the same object fails its primary duty — to fix a moment in the memory with the authority of a carved inscription. The Lissajous drift in State 1, the sensor-driven BRDF translation, the differently-seeded candle simulation — these are not responsiveness, they are restlessness, and restlessness is the enemy of ceremony. When the Pantheon's oculus moves light across the floor it does so by a law, not by a state machine; the guest knows the law and trusts it, and that trust is what give
disputes.concession: The discipline of deriving the shimmer roughness from the scanned surface's actual luminance channel — so that watercolor tooth scatters and gouache concentrates — is exactly right: the physics model is reading a physical fact, not inventing one, and that is the only ground on which a generative sys

disputes.objection: The deckled edge drawn on a Wacom in Figma is not a human trace — it is a simulation of a human trace, which is the thing I am against. Pressure sensitivity on a stylus producing a 0.4–1.2px path variation is not the same as cotton fiber tearing against a wet blade; one is a record of making, the other is a record of performing making on a surface that can undo it with cmd-Z. The marble saw-mark kept 'as proof of material' while everything else is stripped to architectural silence is a single relic in a vitrine — it does not prove process, it decorates with the idea of process.
disputes.concession: The rule that the WebGL bloom stops at the plate edge and never crosses into the text field is correct — restraint about where the light is allowed to go is a real structural decision, not a styling choice, and I would take that boundary into my own work.

disputes.objection: The three-act sequence is a screensaver with a libretto attached — darkness, carry, radiance is a cinematic metaphor dressed as a motion system, but it has no rule that changes with input; the 1.8-second cubic-bezier with two scripted stutters is a recorded performance, not a behaviour, and once you have seen it once you have seen it every time, which is the definition of a loop masquerading as drama. The foil shimmer 'activating at full luminosity' is purely sequential decoration — it does not respond to device state, ambient light, user velocity, or any signal from the world; it fires on a timer, which means it is not a system, it is a gif with better rendering. disputes.concession: The normal-map anchored to the actual scanned paper grain so that shimmer travels along real material ridges is exactly the kind of physical-to-computational binding I would defend — it is a rule derived from a real surface, and that is the correct direction.

disputes.objection: The Minimalist calls the Verde Guatemala marble 'texture' and the deckled edge 'drawn' as if naming the material settles the question of permission and provenance — Verde Guatemala is quarried in a specific region of the Guatemalan highlands, and dropping a photograph of it into 36 wedding evites without naming the quarry, the region, or whether anyone along that extraction chain was asked is exactly the kind of move that mistakes aesthetic specificity for ethical specificity; the marble is not decoration-free just because it is unfiltered. The claim that the deco family has 'no applied texture' because the stone photograph *is* the texture is a category trick: a photograph of a place is sti
disputes.concession: The rule that the WebGL bloom stops at the plate edge and never crosses into the text field is the most disciplined motion constraint on this table, and I would take it into any of my own directions without modification.

disputes.objection: The three-beat sequence — fade, bloom, text — is not drama, it is a checklist performed quietly, and calling that sequence 'ceremony' is the precise alibi I will not accept: ceremony without scale, without the held breath before the curtain, without the moment that is bigger than its container, is just procedure dressed in linen. The art plate never touching the text column edges, the foil bloom stopping obediently at the plate boundary, the gyroscope drift capped at six pixels — these are not decisions about feeling, they are decisions about tidiness, and tidiness is not the same thing as intention. A reveal that refuses to cross its own drawn border has already told the audience that nothi
disputes.concession: The quarry saw-mark left in the Verde Guatemala marble — one specific, undisguised sign of extraction kept visible in every deco card — is exactly right: that is a human trace that earns its place not as texture but as argument, and I would fight to keep it against anyone on this team who called it

disputes.objection: Three acts of arrival is one act too many — the darkness-reveal-radiance sequence is a narrative imposed on the guest before they have chosen to receive it, and the cubic-bezier stutter at 40% and 75% is decoration wearing the costume of authenticity; candlelight hesitates because of physics, not because a timeline was authored to perform hesitation. The 60/40 shadow split, the proscenium spine, the lectern light pool — these are compositional decisions that have already made every emotional choice on behalf of the work, leaving the painting nothing to do but confirm what the motion already announced.
disputes.concession: The insistence that the foil shimmer travel along the actual scanned paper grain — a real normal map derived from a real surface, not a procedural substitute — is exactly right, and I would keep that constraint in any direction I built.

synthesis.direction: One proportional canon — Van de Graaf page margins at 2:3:4:6, golden-section text block, 16-unit baseline grid — governs all 36 designs across three families (botanical, villa, deco), so the line reads as chapters of a single codex, not a mood-board. Art plates are original physical paintings — watercolor on Fabriano, gouache on gesso board, gilded ink on black Canson — drum-scanned at 1200dpi; the scan is the image, no stock, no generative fill. Motion opens static for 1.2 seconds, then: foil shimmer derived from the scanned surface's actual luminance channel (watercolor tooth scatters, gouache concentrates), foreground cutouts drift 4–8px on tilt at breath scale, candle flicker pulses at an irregular 0.3Hz seeded differently each open — stillness first, always. Reduced motion suppresses all animation; the card remains complete.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The FUTURIST's discipline of deriving foil shimmer roughness from the scanned surface's actual luminance channel — so the physics model reads a physical fact rather than inventing one — replaces the CLASSICAL plan for a uniform foil plane and must be built into the WebGL layer for all three families.
synthesis.editorCut: The RADICAL_MINIMAL editor removed the CLASSICAL's 1.2-second pre-motion hold as a hard rule and replaced it with a load-state that simply presents the fully-composed card at full opacity — no authored pause, no countdown — because a scripted silence is still a performance, and the card's stillness should be structural, not timed. The editor also cut the BAROQUE's three-act darkness-to-radiance sequence, which the team majority agreed was a narrative imposed on a guest who opened a link, not a c
synthesis.openDecision: Do the 36 designs commission three dedicated painters — one botanical specialist, one architectural gouachist, one gilding artist — under a Plajah work-for-hire agreement, accepting the cost and timeline that entails; or does the line open with one family fully painted and the other two built from a documented-source hybrid (scanned archival prints, licensed field photography) to reach market fast
synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team was not evenly split — it was split on a single fault line: whether the motion layer is a rule-governed physics model that produces a different state every second, or a fixed, authored sequence that can be re-experienced as the same object. The Futurist argued for the state machine; the Classical Mind argued that a wedding invitation that cannot be re-experienced identically fails its primary duty. I took the Classical side, and I'll tell you why: the weight the brief asks for — letterpress on a phone — comes from fixity, not responsiveness. The Pantheon's oculus moves light by a law the guest can trust. A state machine that reseeds on every open is restless, and restlessness is the enemy of ceremony.

That said, I kept one thing from the Futurist that the Classical proposal did not have: the foil shimmer must be derived from the scanned surface's actual luminance channel, not applied as a uniform plane. Watercolor tooth scatters the shimmer; smooth gouache concentrates it. That constraint — the physics model reading a real material fact — is what separates the WebGL layer from a filter. The Radical Minimalist edited out the scripted 1.2-second pre-motion pause and the Baroque's darkness-reveal sequence; both were performances of stillness rather than structural stillness, and the editor was right to cut them.

The World-Eclectic Traveler raised a provenance objection that the team did not fully resolve: if the deco family uses a specific stone — Verde Guatemala marble was proposed — the quarry, region, and extraction chain need to be named in production notes, not just the aesthetic. I'm flagging that as a production requirement, not a debate to reopen.

One decision remains yours. The entire line's authority rests on original painted art plates, but commissioning three specialist painters under work-for-hire, with drum scans, before a single design ships is a real budget and timeline commitment. You can open with one fully painted family and build the other two in a second phase, or you can commit all three families to the same production standard from day one. That choice determines the line's launch scope and its price ceiling. Everything else the team has agreed on.
